h1: Sportsbook trading infrastructure for regulated operators
secondaryKeywords: real-time odds pricing, sportsbook exposure control, betting platform architecture
contentIdea: A regulated sportsbook loses money in the seconds between a market moving and the book reacting, and it loses its licence over limits that were enforced by hand. Argue that both problems are architectural rather than staffing problems: pricing, exposure and limit enforcement have to sit on one event-driven core that reacts as the market state changes, instead of on trading screens that people watch. Smartbet builds that core.
productDescription: Smartbet builds infrastructure architecture for regulated sportsbook operators. The stack covers real-time pricing, exposure control, event-driven architecture, market state orchestration and automated limit enforcement. Source: smartbet.do. No pricing, implementation timeline or integration list is published, so do not state one.
writingPreferences: Address the reader as "you" and assume they are a CTO or head of trading at a licensed operator. Use "operator" rather than "bookmaker". Do not name any regulator, licence regime or jurisdiction, and do not state any latency, throughput or uptime number — none has been supplied. Keep the proof section short rather than padding it.
